{{Short description|Method of argument}}
'''Anangeon''' ({{langx|grc|ἀναγκαῖον}}, "necessary"),<ref>[http://rhetoric.byu.edu/figures/A/anangeon.htm ''Anangeon'', Silva Rhetoricae, Brigham Young University] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160702031523/http://rhetoric.byu.edu/figures/A/anangeon.htm |date=July 2, 2016 }}</ref> also known as '''dicaeologia''' ({{lang|grc|italic=yes|δικαιολογία}}, "a plea in defense"),<ref>[http://rhetoric.byu.edu/figures/D/dicaeologia.htm ''Dicaeologia'', Silva Rhetoricae, Brigham Young University] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141117031657/http://rhetoric.byu.edu/figures/D/dicaeologia.htm |date=November 17, 2014 }}</ref> is a specious method of argument, in which the basis lies in inevitability or necessity.{{cn|date=August 2019}} For example, a murderer could argue that his actions were inevitable or necessary because the opposite provoked so he had to retaliate ignoring the fact there were alternative actions to handle the situation.  It is used to limit or contradict fault in a matter.

Anangeon can be seen as a part of [[logos]] and is a type of [[non sequitur (logic)|non sequitur]].
